subject.title: [Feature]: Core-owned durable channel ingress drain — unify Telegram spool/fence/adoption lifecycle into a channel-agnostic seam

question: Should https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/104318 sponsor this durable drain/adoption design as its Phase 2 ingress engine, and should Telegram and WhatsApp migrate in one train or as staged pilots?
rationale: The direction matches repository architecture, but it introduces a public plugin seam and changes message-delivery, recovery, and interruption ownership across mature channels; code inspection alone cannot choose the permanent contract or rollout strategy.

options.title: Stage contract and pilots
options.body: Approve the architecture, first lock the core lifecycle contract and invariants, then migrate Telegram and WhatsApp in separately proven shippable steps.

options.title: One coordinated migration
options.body: Approve a single change that introduces the core worker and moves both existing durable channels together, accepting the larger review and rollback surface.

options.title: Continue channel-local hardening
options.body: Do not sponsor the new core seam yet and keep reliability repairs within existing channel implementations while the broader adapter program matures.

recommendation.title: Stage contract and pilots
recommendation.body: Approve the architecture, first lock the core lifecycle contract and invariants, then migrate Telegram and WhatsApp in separately proven shippable steps.

likelyOwner.reason: This person authored the broader ChannelAdapter v2 program that already names the single-ingress-engine phase and has recent merged history in the Telegram adoption path.
